headline: HOT CHILI DRILLS 203m AT 0.43% CuEq AT LA VERDE — DKP073 and DKP067 Confirm Chile Porphyry Still Growing After 45,000m Program; Maiden Resource Underway
snippet: Hot Chili (ASX: HCH, TSX-V: HCH) released fresh drill results on November 17 confirming La Verde continues to grow after formally completing its 45,000-metre program: hole DKP073 returned 203 metres at 0.43% copper equivalent from just 28 metres depth, and DKP067 hit 150 metres at 0.48% CuEq from 4 metres. Both holes extend mineralization beyond the established discovery footprint, indicating the porphyry remains open in multiple directions. A maiden JORC/NI 43-101 resource estimate is in preparation, with final assays from the program expected by late December 2026.

headline: GOLD BOUNCES $36 FROM 14-MONTH LOW TO $3,868 — 96.6% December Rate-Hike Odds Cap Recovery; Wednesday FOMC Minutes Are the Next Binary Catalyst
snippet: Spot gold recovered to around US$3,868 on Tuesday from Monday's 14-month low of $3,832, as bargain hunters stepped in while financial markets priced a 96.6% probability of a December Fed rate hike — up sharply from 74% two weeks ago following October's hot 0.4% monthly CPI print. Analysts say the upside is structurally capped by a firm dollar, rising real yields, and a consensus bearish macro narrative that has pushed gold roughly 30% below its 2026 record. The minutes from the October 27–28 FOMC meeting drop Wednesday, November 18 at 2:00 p.m. ET; a hawkish read confirming committee support for further hikes could send gold through the $3,800 support level, while any dovish nuance is the primary scenario for a year-end recovery.

headline: COCHILCO: GLOBAL LITHIUM FLIPS FROM 79,000t DEFICIT TO 42,000t SURPLUS IN 2027 — Chile Output Rising to 335,000t; $18,500/t Price Forecast Implies Soft Landing
snippet: Chile's state mining commission Cochilco projects the global lithium market will swing from an 79,000-tonne deficit in 2026 to a 42,000-tonne surplus in 2027, as Chile's output climbs 3.1% to 335,000 tonnes. The forecast implies lithium carbonate prices stabilize near US$18,500 per tonne in 2027 — a soft landing rather than a crash — though forecasters diverge widely, with SMM and Morgan Stanley modelling much larger surpluses. For ASX and TSX-V lithium developers, the data reinforces the near-term bearish case for hard-rock projects while supporting low-cost brine producers that can survive at current prices.

headline: AUSTRAL / HAMMER METALS SCHEME LEGALLY EFFECTIVE NOV 16 — $80.7M Queensland Copper Deal Implements Nov 25; Kalman's 39Mt @ 1.1% CuEq Eyes Rocklands Feed
snippet: Austral Resources' (ASX: AR1) scheme to acquire Hammer Metals (ASX: HMX) became legally effective on November 16 following Federal Court approval on November 13, with Hammer shares suspended the same day; the acquisition implements November 25. The A$80.7 million deal — $0.087 per Hammer share, backed by 99.8% of Hammer shareholders — consolidates Queensland's Cloncurry copper district by bringing Hammer's Kalman copper-gold project (39.2 million tonnes at 1.1% copper equivalent) into the same ownership structure as Austral's existing 3Mtpa Rocklands processing plant.

headline: RARE EARTH SELLOFF DEEPENS AHEAD OF TRUMP-XI SUMMIT — USAR Hits 52-Week Low $6.84; Critical Metals -5%, MP Materials -3% on Policy Uncertainty
snippet: US-listed rare earth stocks extended their November rout on Tuesday as traders positioned ahead of the upcoming Trump-Xi summit, uncertain whether US-China talks might ease or accelerate the rare earth supply standoff that has persisted since China's April 2025 export controls. USA Rare Earth (USAR) fell an additional 7% to touch a 52-week low of $6.84 — down from its year high of $32.80 — while Critical Metals slid 5% and MP Materials dropped 3%. The meeting is watched as a potential pivot on the Chinese controls that have produced a 15–20x price divergence between China domestic and Western spot dysprosium, though analysts say any resolution is unlikely to materially change the structural ex-China supply shortage in the near term.

headline: CHINA'S COPPER SMELTING CAPACITY NEAR A CEILING — Association Flags No Major New Plants Through 2027; TC/RC Squeeze Set to Persist Despite LME Price Weakness
snippet: China's copper industry association has flagged that the country's concentrate-fed primary smelting capacity is approaching a structural ceiling in 2026, with no major new processing facilities expected through 2027. The finding means that even as LME copper falls toward $13,207 per tonne under financial market selling pressure, the physical market constraint remains: Chinese smelters cannot absorb additional concentrate volumes, keeping treatment and refining charges at multi-year lows and sustaining the tight Shanghai physical market. For junior copper developers, the analysis supports a medium-term price floor argument — Chinese copper demand cannot be met by expanding domestic smelting alone, keeping import-price incentives structurally elevated despite near-term macro headwinds.

headline: THESE ASX JUNIORS DEFIED 2026'S BEAR MARKET — Stockhead Names Funded, High-Grade Outperformers; Power Minerals' 88m @ 6.33% TREO Among the Standouts
snippet: Stockhead's November 17 roundup identifies ASX junior miners that have held value or advanced during the 2026 sector selloff, profiling companies where funded multi-hole programs, genuine high-grade results and clean share structures have insulated the stock from the broader rout. Rare earth explorer Power Minerals (ASX: PNN) features prominently, with the Brazilian Morro do Ferro project delivering consistent high-grade intersections including 88m at 6.33% TREO and a project-record 40.5% peak sample. The article argues the common threads across 2026's outperformers are funded programs going into the fall, genuine discovery-stage results, and no warrant overhang suppressing any re-rating.

headline: WEDNESDAY'S FOMC MINUTES COULD RATTLE MINERS AGAIN — 96.6% December Hike Priced In; Hawkish Language on Inflation Would Push Gold Below $3,800
snippet: The minutes from the October 27–28 FOMC meeting drop Wednesday, November 18 at 2:00 p.m. ET — the next major event risk for gold and mining equities. Admiral Markets' preview notes that CME FedWatch shows 96.6% odds of a quarter-point rate hike at the December 9 meeting, up from 74% just two weeks ago; hawkish language confirming broader committee support for December and beyond could push gold below its $3,800 support and add fresh pressure to mining equities already down sharply from 2026 peaks. The minority upside risk is a dovish reading where policymakers leave room for a pause — the year-end recovery catalyst the gold sector has been waiting for since October's hot CPI print reversed the rally.

headline: WHY GOLD MINERS FALL HARDER THAN GOLD — Discovery Alert Breaks Down the Operating Leverage Trap Hitting TSX-V and ASX Stocks in 2026
snippet: Discovery Alert's latest analysis explains why gold mining equities are falling 30–40% harder than the gold price itself in the current bear market, breaking down how operating leverage — the same mechanism that magnifies gains in bull markets — amplifies losses as gold approaches miners' all-in-sustaining cost thresholds. The piece identifies which TSX-V and ASX producers and developers are most exposed at current price levels, and argues that investors who understand the mechanism can distinguish between companies experiencing temporary valuation compression and those facing genuine viability risk as gold tests the $3,800 support level.
